title: Mentor to Microlead — 30-day activation checklist and handoff
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a lightweight playbook for converting a strong IC + mentor into a first-time microlead (ship-owner for a 3–6 person pod). It bundles: a backfill hiring plan, an interview rubric for the microlead role and their first direct report, a compact 30-day activation checklist, success metrics, and a template for the 30-day calibration conversation.

Scope and assumptions:
- Microlead = IC with people/triage/roadmap stewardship for a small feature pod; not a people manager with direct compensation responsibilities.
- Target audience: People Ops partnering with Eng Managers and the mentor transitioning into the role.
- This is intentionally pragmatic and checklist-driven so hiring/eng teams can iterate.

Owner & timeline:
- People Ops owner: Priya Menon (this doc)
- Suggested start: announcement week (T-0) -> 30-day activation period -> 60/90 checkpoints.

High-level goals for the first 30 days:
- Establish cadence and trust with pod (1:1s scheduled, 3 retro/action items completed).
- Deliver a small non-blocking ship (bugfix/opt or small A/B) or unblock one feature flow end-to-end.
- Hire/backfill plan launched if mentor vacates a critical IC seat.
- Demonstrate ownership of triage/incidents and a predictable on-call handover runbook.

Success metrics (examples to calibrate with manager):
- People & process: 4+ positive check-ins from peers in feedback survey after 30 days (5-question pulse).
- Delivery: At least one measurable product/infra outcome assigned and closed; PR merged with review lead.
- Ops: Reduced mean time to acknowledge (MTA) on pod incidents by 15% relative to previous sprint (if applicable).

Backfill hiring plan (if mentor role vacated):
1) Immediate: Create a short job spec focusing on system scope, coding impact area, and mentoring responsibilities. Label as "short-term backfill — 6–9 month" if moving fast.
2) Interview loop (fast-track): 1: screening (30m) -> 2: technical pairing (60m) -> 3: design/problem (60m) -> 4: team fit + mentorship philosophy (45m).
3) Offer target window: 7–14 calendar days from first interview to offer.
4) People Ops actions: pre-approved comp range, hiring brief, candidate scorecard template (see rubric section).

Interview rubric (microlead hire and the microlead’s first report) — single-page summary to attach to JD:
Scoring: 1–5 (1 = below bar, 3 = meets, 5 = strong exceed). Aim for average >= 3.5 across core dimensions.
Core dimensions (weights in parentheses):
- Technical depth (35%): systems design, debugging, code quality. Sample probe: "Walk me through a recent latency incident you owned — what did you do to triage and prevent recurrence?"
- Execution & prioritization (25%): shipping small-to-medium features, roadmap tradeoffs. Probe: "Given two high-impact bugs and one small customer request, how do you choose?"
- Coaching/mentorship (20%): past mentoring examples, giving feedback. Probe: "Tell me about a time you helped an engineer move from reactive to proactive ownership."
- Communication & stakeholder management (15%): written/async, triage calls. Probe: "How do you communicate risks to PMs and Eng Managers when delivery timeline slips?"
- Inclusion & collaboration (5%): conflict handling, psychological safety. Probe: "How do you ensure quieter voices are heard during syncs?"

Calibration guidance for interviewers:
- Use anchored notes: cite example evidence (URLs to PRs, postmortems).
- Look for concrete mentoring behaviors (paired programming, feedback cycles) rather than abstract statements.
- For internal candidates moving from mentor -> microlead, weight coaching examples higher and technical depth >= 3.

30-day activation checklist (detailed timeline)
T-3 days (pre-start):
- Announcement + role brief sent to pod and stakeholders. People Ops preps offer/backfill notes.
- Create calendar placeholders: weekly microlead-pod sync (30m), office hours (1hr), 1:1s with each pod member (30–45m).
- Shared doc: create "pod 30-day playbook" in repo or Confluence with links to code owners, infra runbooks, and major tickets.

Day 0–7 (settling in):
- 1:1s with each direct (listen-only for first two 1:1s; focus on ramp blockers, career goals).
- Shadow current on-call rotation and review past 3 incidents + runbook.
- Review roadmap, outstanding PRs, major customers and stakeholders.
- Update OWNERS or CODEOWNERS for the pod scope where appropriate.
- Quick wins: pick a subtask < 2 days to ship to build confidence.

Day 8–14 (structuring work):
- Establish triage rules and SLAs with team (what gets priority, bug vs feature).
- Run first microlead-pod sync: set agenda template, action log, and owner assignments.
- Introduce pair rotation schedule: two-week pairing blocks for knowledge transfer.
- Identify one mentee to co-own a small feature.

Day 15–21 (driving outcomes):
- Lead a small deliverable end-to-end and document decision log.
- Kick off backfill hiring if needed (job spec posted, recruiter briefed).
- Host a retro for the prior sprint focusing on process improvements; ensure 2–3 concrete actions.

Day 22–30 (review & stabilize):
- Run 30-day calibration meeting with Eng Manager + People Ops: discuss pulse feedback, delivery outcomes, and hire progress.
- Finalize on-call handover docs and incident playbook updates.
- Agree on 60-day goals and 90-day learning plan.

30-day calibration template (30–45 minutes)
Attendees: Microlead, Eng Manager, People Ops partner
Agenda:
- 5m: Quick recap of commitments from T-0
- 10m: People pulse & qualitative signals (what’s going well, what’s concerning)
- 10m: Delivery review (what shipped, blocked items)
- 10m: Hiring/backfill status and decisions
- 10m: Agree 3 priority actions for next 30 days and success definitions

Feedback & evaluation rubric (for the 30-day check-in)
- People: evidence of psychological safety, 1:1 rhythm established (1–5)
- Delivery: measurable outcome (did a feature/bug ship?) (1–5)
- Ops: runbooks updated, incident ownership (1–5)
- Hiring: posted job & first screen scheduled if backfill needed (1–5)
- Overall recommendation: "Continue as-is" | "Support with focused coaching" | "Reassess role fit" (pick one)

Sample communication templates (short):
- Announcement to pod (channel/Slack):
  "Heads-up: Starting Monday, @Name will step into microlead for XYZ pod — they’ll run pod syncs, own triage and the upcoming Q2 small-scope launch. For blockers, ping them in #pod-ops or book 1:1s. People Ops is planning a short handoff doc — reach out if you need context."

- Offer to mentor pair invite (calendar blurb):
  "Kickoff: pairing block with [mentee] to transfer ownership of [area]. Goals: ship a small PR together, review incident runbook, and set next steps."

Risks and mitigation:
- Risk: microlead spends too much time firefighting, not enough on coaching. Mitigation: schedule time-blocked "coaching office hours" and enforce them in calendar.
- Risk: backfill lag causes technical debt. Mitigation: hire fast-track contract for 6–8 weeks as buffer and prioritize knowledge docs.
- Risk: unclear authority boundary with Eng Manager. Mitigation: clarify RACI in 1:1 with manager and add to the pod playbook.

Hiring notes (practical):
- If internal candidate: create an accelerated loop focusing on evidence for coaching and scoped execution; keep comp neutral if lateral.
- For external candidates: explicitly probe mentorship examples and include a short pairing exercise with a current pod member.

Open questions / notes to self (working doc style):
- Should we require microleads to complete a short "leadership fundamentals" async module? (Pros: consistent; Cons: friction).
- Add checklist item to confirm access to all tooling (Kibana, Sentry, deploy keys) before Day 3.
- Consider a short microlead cohort for cross-pod syncs after hire (monthly).

Appendix: sample 5-question pulse (anonymous) to send after 30 days:
1) I feel comfortable raising blockers with the microlead (1–5)
2) The microlead responds to critical issues in a timely way (1–5)
3) The microlead helps clarify priorities for the pod (1–5)
4) I had at least one meaningful coaching interaction in the past month (yes/no)
5) One thing the microlead could improve in the next 30 days (free text)

Last revised notes: Drafted after 3 internal microlead transitions (eng-sre and platform squads) — capture local variations when pairing with Eng Managers.

If this doc is useful, People Ops can templatize as a short Confluence checklist and add to onboarding templates for microleads.
